decisions.reason: The same message independently establishes easy assembly, which is already represented by the candidate's INTRODUCE Event; the added drop-retention constraint does not change assembly usability.
Securing components during a drop does not alter the existing requirement to accommodate three boards and the battery.
The drop-retention constraint does not change the specified sensor-air inlet or outlet locations.
The source does not resolve the display-size ambiguity or change the display cutout, mounting, connection, or cover-installation requirements.
Keeping components in place if dropped does not select or modify either permitted LED light-path method.
The enclosure-level retention rule does not necessarily change the sensor board's orientation, connector placement, board order, or component arrangement.
The source adds an enclosure retention constraint but specifies no change to the main board's dimensions, orientation, connectors, or cable layout.
The existing power-board mounting holes and layout remain valid; the source does not require a particular board-level retention implementation or layout change.
Mechanical drop retention is unrelated to the main-board I2C resistor values, population policy, purpose, and topology.
The enclosure retention rule does not change the battery connector's electrical specification, placement, orientation, or mounting style.
The source does not alter panel-control coverage, GPIO mappings, connector wiring, or button placement.
The mechanical drop-retention decision has no necessary effect on I2C cable length, clock speed, pull-ups, or series-resistor configuration.
